title: DateRangePicker
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.DateRangePicker with androidx.compose.material3.rememberDateRangePickerState, in androidx.compose.material3.DatePickerDialog opened from a MonarchFormField row; MonarchMenu for presets
summary: The Material 3 date range picker, opened in a DatePickerDialog from a button in a MonarchFormField row, with presets in a MonarchMenu, the earliest and latest days as SelectableDates and a longest length checked before Save. The theme gives it Monarch colors, type and shapes; Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: For a period with a first and a last day: a report range, leave, a sprint, a filter on created or due dates. Offer presets such as Last 7 days when people mostly pick common periods.
whenNotToUse: For one date, use the Material 3 DatePicker (see date-picker). For two unrelated dates, use two DatePickers. For a few fixed periods with no custom range, use a MonarchSegmentedControl (see segmented-control) or MonarchSelect.
api: @Composable fun DateRangePicker(state: DateRangePickerState, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, dateFormatter: DatePickerFormatter = remember { DatePickerDefaults.dateFormatter() }, colors: DatePickerColors = DatePickerDefaults.colors(), title: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = …, headline: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = …, showModeToggle: Boolean = true, …)

@Composable fun rememberDateRangePickerState(initialSelectedStartDateMillis: Long? = null, initialSelectedEndDateMillis: Long? = null, initialDisplayedMonthMillis: Long? = initialSelectedStartDateMillis, yearRange: IntRange = DatePickerDefaults.YearRange, initialDisplayMode: DisplayMode = DisplayMode.Picker, selectableDates: SelectableDates = DatePickerDefaults.AllDates): DateRangePickerState

@Composable fun DatePickerDialog(onDismissRequest: () -> Unit, confirmButton: @Composable () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, dismissButton: @Composable (() -> Unit)? = null, …, content: @Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit)
interface SelectableDates { fun isSelectableDate(utcTimeMillis: Long): Boolean; fun isSelectableYear(year: Int): Boolean }
@Composable fun MonarchFormField(label: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, …, helperText: String? = null, errorText: String? = null, …, control: @Composable (controlModifier: Modifier) -> Unit)

states.name: empty
states.description: The field's button reads "Choose dates"; the dialog opens with no day selected.

states.name: chosen
states.description: The button shows the first and last day in the locale's medium format; the dialog opens with the range highlighted from start to end.

states.name: half chosen
states.description: In the dialog the first tap sets the start and the second the end; until both are set the app keeps Save disabled, so a filter never runs on half a range.

states.name: limited
states.description: Days SelectableDates rejects (before the earliest or after the latest day) are dimmed and cannot be chosen; yearRange limits the years.

states.name: too long
states.description: The app disables Save while the range is longer than its longest length, and says the limit in the field's helper text.

states.name: input mode
states.description: The mode toggle switches to two typed date fields in the locale's pattern, validated by Material 3, which also reports an end before the start.

states.name: disabled
states.description: MonarchFormField(enabled = false) and a disabled button; the dialog cannot open.

appearance: The dialog uses the raised surface with extra-large corners; the start and end days sit on the accent solid circle with on-solid text, the days between on the accent subtle band, today is outlined in the accent role and disabled days use the disabled text role, all from MonarchTheme in the light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: Planned and kept as native: Material 3 has a range picker, and an Android user expects it (Google Calendar, Settings). The web DateRangePicker is a single field with two typed inputs and a one- or two-month calendar that previews the range as the pointer moves, with presets, minimum and maximum lengths, week numbers and day dots. On Android the Material 3 DateRangePicker is a full-height scrolling calendar (in a DatePickerDialog, or full screen) with its own typed input mode; presets are a MonarchMenu beside the field and call DateRangePickerState.setSelection; the earliest and latest days are SelectableDates; a shortest or longest length is checked by the app before Save, because SelectableDates cannot depend on the chosen start. Values are epoch milliseconds at UTC midnight (selectedStartDateMillis, selectedEndDateMillis), both ends inclusive, not ISO strings. Week numbers and day dots are not offered by Material 3; for those use MonarchMiniMonth. iOS builds MonarchDateRangePicker, Start and End rows of system date pickers, because iOS has no range calendar.
accessibility: System behavior: the dialog is a window with its own title, so TalkBack moves into it and returns to the field's button when it closes.
System behavior: each day is a button read with its full date and whether it is the start, the end, in the range, today or disabled.
System behavior: the input mode has two labelled text fields whose errors are read by TalkBack.
The field's button is a MonarchButton with a 48dp target, labelled by MonarchFormField, and its text says the range or "Choose dates".
Preset items are MonarchMenuItem buttons; Save is a ghost MonarchButton read as disabled while the range is incomplete or too long.
Font scale and right-to-left calendars are handled by Material 3.
edgeCases: selectedStartDateMillis and selectedEndDateMillis are UTC midnights: formatting them in the device zone can show the previous day west of UTC.
A range of one day has the same start and end; the user taps the same day twice.
The state is remembered once: after a preset, call setSelection so the dialog opens on the preset range.
The dialog is tall; give DateRangePicker Modifier.weight(1f) inside DatePickerDialog so its months scroll.

examples.title: Report period with presets

parityExceptions.reason: The web shows one box holding the two typed dates, a clear button and a calendar button, with the presets inside its popover. Android shows the same box (dates, clear, calendar) and opens the system date range picker in a dialog on tap; the dates are picked on the calendar there, not typed, and the presets are a Presets menu in the dialog's action row. The label, the date format and the helper line are the web's.
parityExceptions.convention: Material 3 DateRangePicker dialog; dates are picked, not typed
